guide.title: ECG Acquisition — 12-Lead
guide.lead: A good 12-lead starts with good skin contact and the right intercostal spaces. Get it within 10 minutes of first contact for chest pain, add right-sided and posterior leads when the pattern asks for them, and transmit early.

steps.title: Find the 4th space
steps.text: Angle of Louis = 2nd rib; the space below is the 2nd intercostal space; count down to the 4th.

steps.title: V1 and V2
steps.text: 4th intercostal space, right and left of the sternum.

steps.title: V5 and V6
steps.text: Same level as V4: anterior and mid-axillary lines.

steps.title: Breasts
steps.text: Place V3–V6 under the breast tissue, not on it; after mastectomy, use the same landmarks.

steps.title: Limbs
steps.text: RA, LA, RL, LL on the limbs (or shoulders and hips).

sections.title: Extra leads
rows: V4R: right 5th intercostal space, mid-clavicular – RV infarction
V7–V9: posterior, same level as V6 – posterior MI

sections.title: Artifact
rows: Better skin prep and contact; reduce movement and breathing motion
Warm the patient, support the arms, ask them to relax
notes: Skin prep: clip hair, alcohol or abrasion, dry, press electrodes firmly.

quiz.q: 12-lead has a wandering baseline in several leads. First step?
options: Re-prep the skin and reapply electrodes firmly; reduce movement
quiz.explanation: Most artifact is contact or movement.

quiz.q: V1 was placed in the 2nd intercostal space. Error?
options: V1 belongs in the 4th space right of the sternum
quiz.explanation: High V1/V2 is the commonest error.

quiz.q: Inferior ST elevation with ST depression in V3–V4. Extra leads?
options: V4R for RV involvement and V7–V9 for posterior MI

quiz.q: Time goal for a 12-lead in suspected ACS:

quiz.explanation: V5 and V6 at the same level.

options: Posterior chest at the level of V6
quiz.explanation: Posterior axillary line to beside the spine.

quiz.q: Fine regular interference on all leads with a heater running nearby:
options: Mains (50 or 60 Hz) interference: unplug devices

quiz.q: Female patient: where do V3–V6 go?
quiz.explanation: Breast tissue lowers voltage and shifts position.

options: Clip hair, clean, dry, press electrodes firmly

flashcards.question: V1
flashcards.answer: 4th intercostal space, right of the sternum. Find the angle of Louis (2nd rib) and count down.

flashcards.question: V4
flashcards.answer: 5th intercostal space, mid-clavicular line; V5 and V6 on the same level.

flashcards.question: Limb leads
flashcards.answer: RA, LA, RL (ground), LL – on the limbs or on the shoulders and lower abdomen.

flashcards.question: Most common placement error
flashcards.answer: V1 and V2 too high (2nd or 3rd intercostal space).

flashcards.question: Diagnostic-quality ECG
flashcards.answer: Skin prep: clip hair, clean, dry, press electrodes firmly; still, warm, relaxed patient.

flashcards.question: Four kinds of artifact
flashcards.answer: Wandering baseline (contact, movement), mains interference (50 or 60 Hz), muscle tremor, lead off.

flashcards.question: Right-sided V4R
flashcards.answer: In every inferior STEMI to look for RV infarction (before nitrates).

flashcards.question: Posterior leads V7–V9
flashcards.answer: When V1–V3 show ST depression: possible posterior MI.

critical.scenario: Chest pain radiating to the jaw; he's shivering in a cold ambulance and keeps lifting his arms to talk. The tracing is coarse and irregular.
critical.question: Best sequence?

options.t: Warm him, support his arms, re-prep the skin, ask him to relax and breathe slowly, then repeat the 12-lead

critical.kpi: Troubleshoots artifact to obtain a diagnostic 12-lead

critical.scenario: 72-year-old with syncope after bilateral mastectomy with prostheses; you need a 12-lead.
critical.question: How do you adjust?

options.t: Remove the prostheses, use standard landmarks (4th and 5th spaces) and note any adjustments on the tracing

critical.kpi: Adapts lead placement to patient anatomy

critical.scenario: Chest pain call; your partner reminds you of the 10-minute ECG goal. The patient is sitting up, talking, mildly distressed.
critical.question: Most efficient approach?

options.t: Partner sets up the monitor and electrodes while you take the history; expose the chest with privacy; acquire and transmit early
Full history first, then the ECG

critical.kpi: Acquires a 12-lead within 10 minutes of contact
